tei:titleStmt.tei:title: ברכת המזון לפסח
A poetic Birkat haMazon for Pesaḥ, from the Cairo Geniza (CUL T-S H11.88 1v)

tei:div.tei:head: A poetic Birkat haMazon for Pesaḥ, from the Cairo Geniza (CUL T-S H11.88 1v)

tei:lg.tei:l: Blessed are You,
Cause, our God,
Sovereign of Eternity,
who feeds the world entire...
The nation whose eyes are pools
was crushed with pitch and bricks.
The Proud One peered at her through her lattice,
knocking for her with healing and remedy.
So, at midnight, then They passed over,
and fulfilled the statement They conversed.
This God of mine passed over the entrances,
graced them in eating the Pesaḥ offering.
As it is written:

And you will say, it is the pesaḥ offering for the Cause who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when smiting Egypt, and saved our homes. And the people bowed and prostrated. (Exodus 12:27)
And it is said:
You open Your hand and sate all life as willed. (Psalms 145:15)
Blessed are You, Cause,
who feeds all.
Massacring the first-virility of the Lydians,
they went out crushed with wealth from the slave-house.
All say “Glory!” and there stand in awe —
thus They redeemed them from enslaving.
From stresses You brought them out,
the souls that You freed.
Eternal the covenant You cut with them,
for the law and land that You bequeathed them.
As it is written:
a land of wheat and barley and grapes and figs and pomegranates; a land of olive oil and honey. (Deuteronomy 8:8)
And it is said:
And you will eat and be sated and bless the Cause your God for the good land that was given you. (Deuteronomy 8:10)
Blessed are You, Cause,
for the land and for the food.
Freed, they composed songs
as the Tanites drowned in the breaking-waves.
Your communities went out in songs,
singing cheer and praise.
Boundary-Setter, free us on this day,
as You — awesome and terrific — freed.
Build there the city, from the day
you will delight us with the joy of this day.
As it is written:
This day the Cause made; let us cheer and rejoice on it. (Psalms 118:24)
Our God and God of our ancestors,
may these ascend and come and arrive and be seen
and be desired and be heard and be accounted and be remembered:
our memories and our accounts,
and the memory of our ancestors,
and the memory of the anointed son of David Your servant,
and the memory of Jerusalem Your holy city,
and the memory of all Your people the house of Israel before you,
for survival, for goodness,
for grace, for kindness, and for compassion,
for life, and for peace,
on this pilgrimage of matsah.
Remember us on it, Cause our God, for good,
and account us on it for blessing,
and save us on it for life.
And by word of salvation and compassion,
have mercy and grace and compassion on us
and save us,
for our eyes turn to You,
for a merciful compassionate Sovereign God are You.
And it is said:
Rebuilding Jerusalem is the Cause; gathering the exiles of Israel. (Psalms 147:2)
Blessed are You, Cause,
who builds Jerusalem, amen, in our lives.

tei:note.tei:p: Literal Hebrew: Zoanites. Tsoꜥan, or Zoan, is nearly universally agreed to be equivalent to the ancient Egyptian city of Tanis.
See Pirkei d’Rebbi Eliezer for an explanation of this translation of Shaddai.
